correctness.rationale: The rational functional calculus is defined for every h>=0 because the Pade denominator roots have positive real part and all Q eigenvalues have nonpositive real part. Exact inversion modulo x^8-1 gives all eight circulant coefficients. The four potentially signed numerator factors are verified by exact polynomial identities, with a single positive root apiece by one Descartes sign change and the intermediate value theorem. Positive-coefficient numerators give the remaining four classes, and rational endpoint tests order the unique roots so that their simultaneous nonnegative set is exactly [ell,u]. The c7 and c1 signs exclude respectively all h in (0,ell) and (u,infty), T(0)=I, row/column conservation holds. The actual embedded verifier runs exact symbolic identities and direct matrix inversions. Numerical tests do not substitute for the all-h argument.

originality.rationale: The all-timestep exact positivity interval for the canonical irreducible uniform directed eight-cycle is a new, specific classification relative to inspected source statements: unlike the known absorbing pure-birth eight-state witness, it is irreducible, regular and doubly conservative, and its lower and upper boundary polynomials and numerical values differ. Classical general Pade negativity and zero absolute-monotonicity radius do not determine a nontrivial recovered stochasticity interval or its endpoints. Verified against own recoverable prior finding titles/claims and actual public record searches. Potential unindexed exact cyclic computations remain a residual risk, not a demonstrated stronger covering theorem.

value.rationale: The eight-state dimension is the sharp first size where the fourth-order Pade endpoint map can fail small-step Markov positivity; the canonical irreducible and balanced directed ring tests whether the phenomenon survives without absorption or boundary effects. The complete all-time classification identifies exact entrywise-positive recovery then eventual loss on a natural circulant stochastic generator, with two distinct algebraic thresholds and one direct useful timestep admissibility rule. This is a motivated finite model from the minimal-obstruction problem, not arbitrary parameter sampling, and distinguishes conservation and irreducibility from more general known examples.
